A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIGER/EchoSet work. All 18 pages, including Appendices A–I, are readable, and the text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original speech-separation experiments, real-world evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, and cinematic sound-separation results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The TIGER architecture, band splitting, shared FFI blocks, MSA and F3A modules, reconstruction procedure, and training objectives remain unchanged, including the cinematic-task adaptation.

E1.justification: The named datasets and tasks are retained. Appendix A changes the evaluated Libri2Mix variant from noise-free to noisy, but Section 6.2 still describes it as lacking noise. This conflict prevents determining whether actual input-environment coverage changed or only its documentation was revised.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmarks, module-replacement experiments, DnR comparison, and TIGER-tiny comparison against SudoRM-RF + GC3.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the stated 16 kHz Libri2Mix min setting from 'no noise or reverberation' to 'with noise and without reverberation.' This is a limited reported protocol revision; it does not establish that experiments were rerun. Other settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The band-split, module-removal, sequence-model replacement, and time-frequency interleaving ablations are retained unchanged, as are the lightweight-model analysis and spectrogram examples.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains timing averages over 1,000 forward and backward passes. Neither version reports additional training seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported scores, rankings, and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 2 retains TIGER-large's Libri2Mix SDRi/SI-SDRi values of 18.34/17.97 dB. No revised results accompany the changed noise-setting description.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), the mathematical model descriptions, and the appendix band-split reasoning remain unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about TIGER's efficiency, performance in complex acoustic environments, and EchoSet's realism and generalization benefits.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability statements remain unchanged. In particular, Section 6.2 still attributes Libri2Mix's relative simplicity to the absence of noise and reverberation, despite the revised appendix description.

D1.justification: Appendix A revises the reproducibility-relevant description of whether the selected Libri2Mix inputs contain noise. Hyperparameters, hardware, processing instructions, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to previous speech-separation methods and datasets are unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the Libri2Mix setting sentence and the arXiv version/date stamp. Section organization, terminology, and the remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–12 retain their designs, captions, and placement. The overall page layout is preserved; there are no added, removed, or redesigned displays.

improvement.justification: The Appendix A revision aligns the selected Libri2Mix setting with the general noisy-dataset description in Section 2 and Table 1, but conflicts with Section 6.2's unchanged noise-free description. All results remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish which condition produced those results, so it is unclear whether the edit corrects an earlier error or introduces one, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
